title: VP of Product Development

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: General Formulations already manufactures GF 108 Tedlar overlaminate and actively co-develops anti-graffiti solutions with DuPont. The VP of Product Development would be the strategic decision-maker for expanding the Tedlar product portfolio beyond GF 108 into new applications. With GF showcasing Economy Film & Laminate Solutions at ISA 2025 and launching products like GF 767 Sparkle Holographic Film, this role is actively managing product innovation and differentiation. They would care about: (1) expanding premium product lines with proven 10-20 year durability claims to command higher margins, (2) competitive differentiation in the crowded pressure-sensitive media market, (3) leveraging the existing Tedlar partnership to develop new SKUs for architectural, wall protection, and transit interior applications where GF has manufacturing capacity but limited Tedlar penetration, (4) reducing warranty exposure and customer complaints by upgrading additional product lines to Tedlar-grade durability. This role owns the product roadmap and portfolio strategy that would drive incremental Tedlar adoption across GF's 400,000+ sq ft manufacturing capacity serving US, Canada, LATAM, and APAC markets.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: This VP of Product Development owns the strategic product roadmap and portfolio decisions for General Formulations' entire pressure-sensitive media line. They have decision authority over which materials and technologies get integrated into new SKUs, manage product innovation cycles, and are accountable for product differentiation strategy in a crowded market. Given GF's recent launches (GF 767 Sparkle Holographic Film, Economy Film & Laminate Solutions at ISA 2025), this role is actively driving new product development. They likely report to the President/CEO and collaborate closely with Sales, Operations, and Marketing leadership to ensure new products meet market demands while maintaining manufacturing feasibility and margin targets.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Beyond the existing GF 108 anti-graffiti laminate, this VP should care about expanding Tedlar into: (1) Wall protection and covering applications—GF serves the architectural graphics market but may be using less durable alternatives where Tedlar's scratch resistance, cleanability, and mold/mildew resistance would enable premium positioning, (2) Transit and rail interiors—GF already wraps LA Metro buses externally with MetroMark 209; adding Tedlar-backed interior wall panels or protective films would capture a higher-margin segment with strict fire/smoke requirements, (3) Architectural panel overlaminates—GF's building facade customers need weatherability and fade resistance that Tedlar delivers better than competitive PET or PVC laminates, (4) Premium vehicle wrap overlaminates—expanding beyond the training-focused GF 830 AutoMark Cast to offer a Tedlar-protected version for fleet customers demanding verifiable warranties and reduced replacement cycles.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: This VP likely owns KPIs around: (1) Product portfolio profitability and gross margin expansion—Tedlar-backed SKUs command premium pricing and higher margins than commodity laminates, (2) New product launch success and market adoption rates—expanding Tedlar into additional applications gives them differentiated offerings to drive growth, (3) Warranty claim rates and product quality metrics—upgrading more SKUs to Tedlar reduces field failures from UV degradation, cracking, and graffiti damage, directly improving their product performance scorecard, (4) Competitive win rates against 3M, Avery Dennison, and other pressure-sensitive media suppliers—Tedlar's proven outdoor performance provides a technical advantage they can leverage in customer presentations and RFP responses. This person's career success depends on building a product portfolio that balances innovation, profitability, and market share growth—Tedlar expansion directly supports all three objectives.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: General Formulations just co-exhibited with DuPont Tedlar at ISA Expo 2025 (April 23-25) featuring jointly developed anti-graffiti products, making this the perfect moment to continue the partnership conversation while momentum is high. They're also preparing for PRINTING United Expo 2025, where they'll be showcasing their latest innovations—NOW is when product roadmap decisions for 2025-2026 launches are being finalized. Additionally, the company is actively promoting their Economy Film & Laminate Solutions line, suggesting they're looking to expand their addressable market with both value and premium tiers. The existing GF 108 Tedlar success story provides proof of concept, and the recent joint booth activation demonstrates executive alignment between the two companies. This is an account expansion play with warm relationships already in place, not a cold prospect.

personalization_hooks.hook: GF's recent ISA 2025 joint booth activation with DuPont Tedlar and co-developed anti-graffiti solutions demonstrate strong partnership momentum
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference the successful ISA collaboration as a springboard to discuss expanding Tedlar into additional GF product lines beyond GF 108. Frame this as a natural evolution of the partnership—'building on what we achieved together at ISA.' Position yourself as an extension of their product development team, not just a materials vendor.

personalization_hooks.hook: GF manufactures for architectural, wall covering, and transit interior applications but currently only uses Tedlar in the GF 108 anti-graffiti overlaminate
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Position Tedlar expansion as a portfolio gap-fill opportunity. Lead with: 'You've proven Tedlar's performance in anti-graffiti applications—have you considered how the same UV resistance and cleanability advantages could differentiate your architectural wall protection and transit interior products?' Make it about competitive advantage in segments where they're already competing but potentially without the best material solution.

personalization_hooks.hook: VP of Product Development owns margin expansion and product differentiation strategy in a crowded pressure-sensitive media market competing against 3M and Avery Dennison
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Frame Tedlar as a strategic differentiator, not a material spec. Open with their business challenge: 'In a market where everyone offers similar PET and PVC laminates, how do you justify premium pricing and win against 3M on something other than price?' Position Tedlar as the technical advantage that supports defensible margins and changes the competitive conversation from price to total cost of ownership.

recommended_approach: Lead with partnership continuity from ISA 2025—reference the successful collaboration and position this as a strategic product portfolio discussion, not a sales pitch. Emphasize expanding an existing, proven relationship into new applications where GF already has market presence but may lack the material advantage. Frame the conversation around their product roadmap and competitive positioning challenges, offering to share case studies from similar manufacturers who've expanded Tedlar usage across multiple SKUs to drive margin improvement and reduce warranty exposure.
